main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling fish curry in the shared kitchen given smell complaints from A (work calls), B (bedroom) and C (laundry)

A-B.evidence: Turns 2-3: B and A both complain about the smell; turn 10 B backs the night-time concern. B accepts a heads-up deal while A still objects (27, 29), but both remain on the complaining side.

A-C.evidence: C complains of laundry smell (5, 11) and A of the smell for work calls; C accepts the Tue/Thu deal (24-26) while A rejects it (27), but both still object to the smell.

A-D.evidence: D initially refuses (6); proposes weekends (12) and A accepts (13); later A reopens, saying Tue/Thu cooking still harms calls (27, 29), and D questions this (28), leaving the issue unresolved.

B-C.evidence: C says 'She's right' (11) backing B; both reject weekends (15, 16). B accepts a heads-up (19-22) while C says it doesn't help (24), but they stay broadly aligned.

B-D.evidence: D proposes weekends, B says it doesn't help (15); B suggests 'tell me before you start' (19), D agrees (20), B thanks (22).

C-D.evidence: C rejects weekends (16); C asks for cooking on non-laundry days (24), D says 'Okay. I can do that' (25), C thanks (26).
